messages:
alex: Quick question — customer is insisting on a true escrow option for BYOK where they can push a key to our HSM proxy and have a documented custody boundary. they flagged PCI/DORA requirements. can we outline the risks and a recommended minimal design?
maria: TL;DR: possible but nontrivial. main concerns: audit trail + separation of duties + emergency access model. we should map who can request key import, who can view metadata, and who can rotate/fallback.
sanjay: +1. also need to confirm what we store: do we persist any key material at rest? ideal is zero key material in our DB. only keep wrapped blobs and KMS/HSM identifiers.
jamie: from infra side: we support an HSM proxy in prod that can accept wrapped key blobs via mTLS. flow we use today: customer -> client-side wrap (KMIP/Azure/GCP/AWS specific) -> upload -> HSM unwrap in enclave. but customers want escrow where we keep a sealed backup in a separate vault.
katie: compliance ask: escrow = we store a decryptable copy. that triggers higher controls: quarterly key access reviews, 3-person approval for recovery, dedicated audit logs with 7+ years retention depending on customer/regulation.
alex: ok. for RBAC, proposal: only principals in group `hsm-ops` can trigger restore, `security-auditors` read-only on audit logs, and `devs` zero access. snippet: ```policy allow { principals: ["group:hsm-ops"] actions: ["hsm:restore"] resources: ["hsm:escrow/*"] } ``` is that too coarse?
maria: don’t hardcode groups in policy blob but fine for discussion. require MFA + justification ticket for any restore. tie every restore to an incident/CSR number and attach audit evidence (who clicked, which key ID, reason).
sanjay: audit logging notes: log collectors must capture: operator id, source IP, kube-pod/container id, API request body hash, HSM response codes, and tz-normalized timestamp. must feed into tamper-evident storage (WORM or write-once S3 lifecycle) for retention.
jamie: integration question: for AWS KMS import token flow we currently support `ImportKeyMaterial`. customers using CloudHSM want a proxy using PKCS#11. we need a mapping doc of supported import flows per provider.
ak: security-bot: New vuln triage: CVE-2026-3344 affecting KMIP client libs. severity: medium-high if using unauthenticated KMIP endpoints. recommended immediate action: ensure KMIP endpoints use mTLS and patch library.
maria: good catch. add to action items: (1) scan all private HSM proxy deployments for KMIP client version, (2) push lib patch to private deploys, (3) validate mTLS cert rotation procedure.
katie: incident response angle: if an escrowed backup is exfiltrated, we need a rapid key compromise playbook: 1) revoke affected key IDs, 2) promote fallback keys, 3) invalidate all wrapped blobs and notify customer with signed proof-of-rotation, 4) audit and escalate to legal/compliance. can someone draft the signed-proof template?
ajamie: I can draft the template. question: do we accept on-behalf imports where customer ops hand keys to our SRE via secure courier? that's a huge compliance red flag for many customers.
sanjay: prefer customer-managed import only (no human handoff). if courier needed, escrow must be flagged as a managed-key product with explicit contract and higher SLA/Security fees.
alex: agree. reduce scope: offer two modes: "direct BYOK" (customer keeps keys, we never store plaintext, only wrapped artifacts) and "escrowed BYOK (managed)" (we store sealed backups with 3-person restore + extra audits + contract).
maria: next steps: write a short architecture note comparing modes, a required controls checklist for escrowed mode (RBAC, audit retention, approval flow, WORM storage), and a vulnerability mitigation checklist. assign owners?
ak: alex -> architecture note draft, maria -> controls checklist, sanjay -> audit pipeline config + KMIP scan, jamie -> provider import matrix + proof template, katie -> compliance wording and legal escalate.
ops-bot: deploybot: scheduled runbook sync queued (runbook-sync/2026-03-18) — will tag changed doc PRs once opened.
alex: thanks. one more: customers ask for a time-limited restore token that expires and requires HSM policy approval to use. can we design that?
maria: yes — short-lived signed attestation from KMS that is single-use. store nonce in WORM log. validate in HSM before unwrap. that'll satisfy most auditors.
sanjay: also add automated sampling audits: nightly job verifies a random 1% of restores have full evidence chain; anomalies create a Sev ticket.
katie: I'll compile compliance checklist and include required contract language for escrowed offering. ETA EOD Friday.
ajamie: I'll start the import matrix doc and mock the signed-proof template by EOD Thursday.
alex: awesome. we'll reconvene after drafts. :thumbsup:
